title: Baseline Localizers and Paired Statistical Comparison (Section 4.3 reference implementation)
description: Single-file C++17 reference implementation of Section 4.3 (baseline methods and the statistical comparison plan) of a dissertation on hybrid Bayesian tactical spatial identification of Wi-Fi signal sources. On a synthetic statistical radiomap it evaluates four localizers on identical inputs: RSSI path-loss trilateration, WKNN fingerprinting, a probabilistic Horus/Roos-style estimator, and a proposed robust variant. Paired errors (grouped in session/site blocks) feed the full plan of Section 4.3.8: block bootstrap 95% confidence intervals of MAE and of paired differences, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with a Hodges-Lehmann median difference, the McNemar test on paired zonal-correct proportions, Cliff's delta effect size, Holm-Bonferroni multiplicity control, and a Friedman statistic with a Nemenyi critical difference. It demonstrates that a statistically significant MAE difference can have a negligible effect size, so lower MAE alone is not a scientific claim. No external dependencies; runs as-is on OnlineGDB. Synthetic illustration, not empirical results; operating points are to_be_validated.
